Load Balancing

1. How Ignite Load Balances Compute Tasks
  • When you submit a compute task with multiple jobs, Ignite distributes jobs across nodes using a load balancing SPI;
  • The goal is to spread work evenly so no single node becomes a bottleneck;
2. Built-in Load Balancing Strategies
StrategyDescription
RoundRobinLoadBalancingSpi (default) Distributes jobs to nodes in round-robin order;
WeightedRandomLoadBalancingSpi Assigns jobs randomly but with configurable weights per node;
AdaptiveLoadBalancingSpi Adapts to node load metrics (CPU, job count); sends more work to less loaded nodes;
3. Configuring Load Balancing
  • // Round-robin (default)
RoundRobinLoadBalancingSpi lbSpi = new RoundRobinLoadBalancingSpi();
lbSpi.setPerTask(true); // round-robin per task (not global)

IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setLoadBalancingSpi(lbSpi);

// Adaptive — based on CPU load
AdaptiveLoadBalancingSpi adaptiveSpi = new AdaptiveLoadBalancingSpi();
adaptiveSpi.setLoadProbe(new AdaptiveCpuLoadProbe());
cfg.setLoadBalancingSpi(adaptiveSpi);
4. Failover
  • If a node fails while executing a compute job, Ignite can automatically retry the job on another node;
  • Failover is handled by the FailoverSpi:
    • AlwaysFailoverSpi (default) — always retries on another node;
    • NeverFailoverSpi — never retries;
    • JobStealingFailoverSpi — steals jobs from overloaded nodes;
  • Configure max failover attempts: 
    AlwaysFailoverSpi failoverSpi = new AlwaysFailoverSpi();
failoverSpi.setMaximumFailoverAttempts(3);
cfg.setFailoverSpi(failoverSpi);
5. Job Stealing
  • Job stealing allows underloaded nodes to "steal" queued jobs from overloaded nodes;
  • Useful when job execution times vary significantly;
  • Requires both JobStealingCollisionSpi and JobStealingFailoverSpi;
